I'm writing up a collection of tips in reducing idle bandwidth consumption in Fedora, mainly so that I don't forget the tips I've collected and to help anyone else reduce Fedora's impact on their bandwidth cap.

Disable automatic checking of repositories

Source :: Archive

While Fedora doesn't automatically update itself, there are a handful of exceptions to this rule. One such exception is automatically refreshing repository info to check for new updates.

You can prevent this function from performing automatically by running the following command:

To disable dnf-makecache.service:

systemctl disable dnf-makecache.service

Also disable the dnf-makecache.timer or the service will be restarted:

systemctl disable dnf-makecache.timer

Also disable gnome packagekit refreshes:

gsettings set org.gnome.software download-updates false

Set your connection as metered in NetworkManager

Source :: Archive

Setting your connection as metered will cause software that respects this setting to treat your connection with kid gloves when necessary, limiting the amount of idle data usage spent on this connection.

Get device's current connection: 

nmcli -t -f GENERAL.CONNECTION --mode tabular device show $DEVICE | tail -n1

Show current metered status:

nmcli -f connection.metered connection show $CONNECTION

Set metered status: 

nmcli connection modify $CONNECTION connection.metered yes

The above tips reduced my idle bandwidth usage from ~3.5mb per hour to a much leaner ~100kb per hour. With a low bandwidth cap and an "on 24/7" media PC, the savings add up.

Bonus tip: Enable low-savings delta updates

Source :: Archive

Fedora utilizes delta updates by default, which means if a package is updated, Fedora will attempt to download just the changed data instead of the entire new package. Fedora has a set package size ratio under which a package qualifies for delta updates.

By default, packages that are at least 25% smaller will quality for delta update. You can modify this requirement in order to increase your system's utilization of delta updates.

To do this, modify the deltarpm_percentage option in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf:

sudoedit /etc/dnf/dnf.conf

On an unmodified dnf.conf, the deltarpm_percentage value will not be present, and your system will interpret this as deltarpm_percentage=75 (which means packages must be at least 25% smaller to quality).

I added the line: 

deltarpm_percentage=90

Which means packages must only be 10% smaller to quality for delta updates.

I hope this helps someone in the same predicament I was in, or anyone looking to reduce their system's idle network footprint. Let me know if you have any corrections, additions, or comments.
